newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma votes again to limit UES investment.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma votes again to limit UES investment.

text.p: Russia's lower house of parliament, the State Duma, voted again to limit foreign investment in Russia's giant power company Unified Energy System (UES) to 25 percent.
The measure must now be approved by the upper house and by President Boris Yeltsin.

Duma deputies cast 338 votes in favour of the bill and no votes against it. Four officals abstained from voting. The lower house had already voted earlier this year to limit foreign investment in UES to 25 percent, but the upper house returned the bill to the Duma for reconsideration.

The text of the bill said the government held a 51 percent stake in the company, which is one of Russia's biggest by market capitalisation and sales. According to UES's annual report, foreign investors own 27.8 percent.

"The Russian government will secure the retention of such a (25 percent) limit on account of the amount of RAO UES shares owned by foreign governments, international organisations, foreign legal bodies and their Russian affiliates and foreign individuals," the bill said.
UES shares were last quoted at $0.3275 on the Russian Trading system at 1240 (0840 GMT), up slightly from their close of $0.3270 on Thursday.
